samples.summary: The `name: CI` spoof this delta closes in mark-ready is still wide open in every `workflow_run` trigger that consumes CI — including the two jobs that push commits with contents:write
samples.evidence:
The delta's stated threat model (checks.mjs:41-56, mark-ready.mjs:133-136, docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1904-1916) is: "anyone able to push a branch to the base repo could add `.github/workflows/anything.yml` with `name: CI` on `push`, get a green run recorded against their own head SHA". Gate 1 now matches on `path`, but every other reader of CI still matches on the run's display name and cannot be fixed by this constant:
- `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:28` — `workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"]`
- `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:21` — same
- `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:19`, `.github/workflows/publish-ghpage.yml:22`, `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:25` — same
The promote path is now protected (mark-ready re-derives gate 1 from the path), but the panel's `fix` job (agent-review-panel.yml:1618-1636, `contents: write`, gated only on `needs.ci.outputs.conclusion == 'success'`, where that conclusion is read off `context.payload.workflow_run.id` at agent-review-panel.yml:291 without ever checking which file produced it) and `agent-iterate-ci.yml` are still driven by a name-matched run. A forged workflow file named `CI` on a branch therefore still starts the LLM fixer, which pushes commits. `github.event.workflow_run.path` is available in the payload and the `ci`/`gate` jobs could assert it against `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH`; the fix belongs in those workflows, not in checks.mjs.

samples.summary: The new "every CI run must be green" rule depends on seeing every run, but both call sites fetch a single unpaginated page of 100
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:129` and `scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:226` both call `actions/runs?head_sha=…&per_page=100` with no `--paginate`. Under the old "newest wins" rule truncation was harmless (the API returns newest-first, so page 1 always held the deciding run). Under `ciConclusion`'s all-must-be-green rule, a red CI run that falls off page 1 is invisible and the gate reads green — the new rule is the thing that makes the missing pagination matter. Unlikely to be hit today (one run per PR head SHA), but the invariant the new code relies on is not enforced at either fetch site.

samples.summary: set-state's lifecycle labelling silently changes semantics with the swap to `ciConclusion` — a run missing `path`, or any second CI run still in flight, now reads as "no CI verdict"
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:228` now delegates to `ciConclusion(runs)`, which returns `null` whenever no run matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` or any matching run is unfinished. `deriveState` (scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:128-129) maps a non-`"success"` conclusion to `agent:awaiting-ci`, so a PR whose SHA has one green and one in-flight CI run — or whose run objects lack `path` for any reason — is now labelled `agent:awaiting-ci` where it previously read `agent:reviewing`. Fail-safe rather than fail-open, but it is a behaviour change to a consumer outside the gate the change was written for, and nothing in `scripts/agent/set-state.test.mjs` exercises `gatherSignals`, so the swap is unobserved there.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim verifies. checks.mjs:40-58 and mark-ready.mjs:133-136 state the exact threat model (a second workflow file with `name: CI` forges the gate) and note that `agent:managed` human PRs — who CAN push workflow files — are on the same path. Name matching is still present at agent-review-panel.yml:28, agent-iterate-ci.yml:21, docker-publish.yml:19, publish-ghpage.yml:22, ci-report.yml:25, and a repo-wide grep for `workflow_run.path` returns no matches, so no workflow asserts the triggering run's file against CI_WORKFLOW_PATH. The panel's `ci` job resolves the run by id alone (agent-review-panel.yml:291 and 301-303) and its conclusion is the only gate on `fix` (agent-review-panel.yml:1618-1636), which holds contents: write; agent-iterate-ci.yml:24-28 with gate at 43-47 likewise pushes with contents: write gated only on conclusion/same-repo/managed. The panel `gate` job (agent-review-panel.yml:176-250) restricts to same-repo agent-managed PRs — exactly the actor class the delta's own comment says is unrestricted — so it does not make the bypass unreachable. In lane for blast radius: CI identity was tightened to a path in the shared reader while other consumers of that same contract, including two contents: write pushing jobs, still resolve it by display name.
